title: Quant Harmony: runtime kernel scorer and headwise lazy-dequant scheduler
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a runtime kernel orchestration layer ("Quant Harmony") that dynamically scores and selects quantization-friendly kernels (INT8/FP8/mixed) per-request and per-attention-head-group, with a headwise lazy-dequant scheduler that amortizes dequant work across microbatches and reuses KV-prefill state when safe. This ticket covers design, prototype implementation, telemetry, benchmarks, and canary rollout for the new scorer + scheduler.

Motivation: Current static routing to INT8 or FP16 kernels results in suboptimal economics: we either pay extra FP16 compute for heads that would run fine in INT8, or we accept dequant overheads that blow up latency on short-decoding queries. By combining a lightweight cost/accuracy scorer with headwise lazy-dequant caching and an amortized decode schedule we aim to reduce per-token cost while holding median and p95 latency within SLOs.

Scope:
- Runtime kernel scorer: cost model that estimates latency and quantization-induced quality delta per kernel variant using recent telemetry and small per-model calibration tables.
- Headwise lazy-dequant scheduler: delay dequantization until the head block is about to execute; share dequant state across microbatches when sequence prefixes are identical or cache-safe.
- Fallback policy: run-time accuracy guard that routes to FP16/FP32 if estimated quality delta crosses a configurable threshold for a request (per-tenant).
- Telemetry hooks: add per-request kernel_choice, score_breakdown, head_error_estimate, amortized_dequant_hits to telemetry.
- Bench harness & dashboards: synthetic workloads (long-context streaming decode, short chat bursts, embedding-prefill) and internal dashboard to track cost/latency/quality.

Non-goals: model weight-level quant rewrites, training-time quant finetuning, or full per-layer automatic quantization suggestions (covered by Optimize).
acceptance_criteria: Kernel scorer integrated into runtime and exposed as a pluggable component (runtime-1.22).
Headwise lazy-dequant scheduler implemented and enabled behind a feature flag.
Observed >=10% token-cost reduction on quant-friendly workloads in canary (weighted by token volume) without >5% regression in median latency or >10% regression in p95 for 99% of requests.
Per-request telemetry emitted for kernel_choice, score_breakdown, head_error_estimate, amortized_dequant_hits.
Canary rollout plan documented and console rollout config created (canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%).
Design doc and benchmark artifacts linked in ticket.
tasks: Draft design doc: quant harmony scoring formula, inputs (histogram of seq lengths, per-layer sensitivity table), and fallback thresholds.
Prototype scorer in Python and validate against offline traces (10k requests).
Implement C++ scorer wrapper and integrate into prefill/decode path.
Implement headwise lazy-dequant state: data structures for deferred dequant, safe-sharing detection, and eviction policy.
Add telemetry fields and wire to observability: logs + structured spans + dashboard metrics.
Create benchmark harness and run A/B experiments across 3 representative models (base, long-context, high-precision).
Implement feature flag and rollout plan in Console; coordinate with Prod and SRE for canary windows.
Code review, perf regression testing, and finalize release notes for runtime-1.22.

P95 increased ~4% on short chat traces; hypothesis: dequant deferral adds tail work for small batches. Will add amortization across microbatches to reduce tail.

Initial telemetry keys added. Ready for internal perf run: https://dash.redwood.ai/boards/quant-harmony/bench-2025-02-28

2025-03-03 - Evelyn Chen (PM): Reviewed canary plan. Proposal: 48h canary at 5% traffic, monitor kernel_choice distribution, amortized_dequant_hits, and p95. If quality regression metric (signal from Eval infra) > 0.5% for targeted prompts, rollback and escalate to Research. Also tag customers with high regulatory impact to keep on FP default.
notes: Design trade-offs: aggressive INT8 preference reduces cost but requires conservative run-time quality checks per-tenant. We'll default to tenant-level tuning knobs exposed in Console.
Open question: Should we persist per-tenant kernel preference across sessions? If yes, we need storage + migration plan (follow-up ticket).
Risk: If amortized sharing incorrectly assumes prefix identity, we could leak stale KV state across requests. Validator added to tasks to ensure strict cache-safety checks.
